clinician.final_diagnosis: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) presenting with recurrent aseptic meningitis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man presented with an 18-year history of 121 episodes of recurrent aseptic meningitis starting at age 53, characterized by prodromal low-grade fever, fatigue, arthralgia, and urticaria followed by high fever and headache. Cerebrospinal fluid demonstrated neutrophilic pleocytosis (>1000 PMN leukocytes/mm3) with negative bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial cultures, negative PCR for herpesviruses and enteroviruses, and negative genetic testing for familial Mediterranean fever (MEFV, MVK) and other autoinflammatory syndromes (TNFRSF1A, NLRP3, NLRP12). Urticarial biopsy showed neutrophil infiltration. Corticosteroids shortened attack duration but did not prevent recurrence. At age 68, he developed severe hemolytic anemia (hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL, lactate dehydrogenase 3004 IU/L). Flow cytometric analysis revealed deficiency of GPI-anchored proteins CD55 and CD59 on erythrocytes and granulocytes, establishing a diagnosis of PNH. Bone marrow examination showed no aplasia or hypoplasia. Following initiation of eculizumab (anti-C5 antibody), all symptoms including urticaria, arthralgia, headache, and hemolysis completely resolved and remained in remission for 3 years.
